note: Figures are as published by each source and are not adjusted. Strait-facing PRC figures are the PLA Eastern and Southern Theaters, the US Defense Department's 'Taiwan Strait area'. Newer editions (2024, 2025) of the DoD report exist but could not be retrieved; carrier and other counts have grown since 2022.

dod2022.label: US DoD, Military and Security Developments Involving the PRC 2022, Appendix I

dod2024.label: US DoD, China Military Power Report 2024 (via A. Erickson's summary)

iiss2024.label: IISS, The Military Balance 2024, as cited by the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (2024 report, ch. 9)

iiss2024res.label: IISS, The Military Balance 2024, p. 315, as cited by Wikipedia

prcbudget.label: Defense News, 10 March 2026 (official PRC budget announced 5 March 2026)

metrics.label: Defence budget
metrics.definition: PRC: official 2026 budget, 1.91 trillion yuan (about $277bn), +7%. Taiwan: proposed 2026 total NT$949.5bn (about $31.2bn, 3.32% of GDP), including special budgets, veterans' affairs and the coast guard, on NATO's method.
metrics.caveat: China's official figure excludes items such as some research and paramilitary spending, so independent estimates (e.g. SIPRI) are higher. Taiwan's figure was still awaiting legislative approval.

metrics.label: Ground force personnel
metrics.definition: Total ground force personnel. PLA total and Eastern and Southern Theaters; Taiwan total.
metrics.caveat: Ground forces only. The DoD's 2024 report gives the PLA 2,035,000 active personnel across all services.

metrics.label: Reserves
metrics.caveat: Different sources and definitions: Taiwan's figure counts everyone with a reserve obligation, most of whom train little. The one category where Taiwan's raw number is larger.

metrics.label: Fighters
metrics.definition: Fighters, PLAAF and PLA Navy aviation combined, excluding fighter trainers. With trainers: PRC 2,900 total, 800 in the two theaters; Taiwan 450.
metrics.caveat: Counts airframes, not generation or readiness. Taiwan's F-16V upgrades and new F-16 Block 70 deliveries post-date some of these figures.

metrics.label: Bombers and attack aircraft
metrics.definition: Bombers and attack aircraft, PLAAF and PLA Navy aviation.

metrics.label: Special mission aircraft
metrics.definition: Special mission aircraft (e.g. early warning, electronic warfare, reconnaissance), as counted by the DoD.
metrics.caveat: Taiwan's count is higher on this definition; category boundaries vary between sources.

metrics.label: Aircraft carriers
metrics.caveat: Out of date: the DoD's 2025 report refers to three Chinese carriers, after Fujian entered service.

metrics.label: Destroyers
metrics.definition: Destroyers. The DoD lists 6 cruisers separately (2 in the two theaters); Taiwan has none.
metrics.caveat: Chinese destroyer numbers have grown since 2022.

metrics.label: Frigates
metrics.caveat: Many of Taiwan's frigates are older hulls acquired from the US and France.

metrics.label: Corvettes
metrics.definition: Corvettes. The DoD gives no theater breakdown.
metrics.caveat: Taiwan has since commissioned Tuo Chiang-class corvettes (six by 2024, per the US-China Commission), which the 2022 table predates.

metrics.label: Amphibious ships
metrics.definition: Tank and medium landing ships and amphibious transport docks, as one line in the DoD table.
metrics.caveat: Almost all Chinese amphibious lift sits in the two theaters facing Taiwan. Civilian ferries and roll-on/roll-off ships could add capacity and are not counted.

metrics.label: Attack submarines (diesel)
metrics.definition: Diesel attack submarines. Separately, the PLA has 9 nuclear attack submarines (2 in the two theaters) and 6 ballistic-missile submarines.
metrics.caveat: Taiwan's two operational boats date from the 1980s; its first indigenous submarine, Hai Kun, was undergoing trials after 2023.

metrics.label: Missile patrol craft
metrics.definition: Coastal patrol craft armed with missiles.

metrics.label: Coast guard ships
metrics.definition: Coast guard ships as counted by the DoD in 2022 (larger vessels).
metrics.caveat: Excludes China's maritime militia, which numbers in the thousands of fishing vessels.

metrics.label: Coast guard patrol and coastal combatants
metrics.definition: Patrol and coastal combatants of the China Coast Guard and Taiwan's Coast Guard Administration (IISS 2024).
metrics.caveat: Broader definition than the DoD line above, so the two are not comparable with each other. Excludes China's Maritime Safety Administration and militia.

metrics.label: Short-range ballistic missiles
metrics.definition: PLA Rocket Force: 200 launchers and 600+ missiles, range 300–1,000 km. The figure is a minimum ('600+').
metrics.caveat: No public figure exists for Taiwan; its strike missiles are mainly cruise missiles, not a comparable ballistic force.

metrics.label: Medium-range ballistic missiles
metrics.definition: PLA Rocket Force: 250 launchers and 500+ missiles, range 1,000–3,000 km. The figure is a minimum ('500+').
metrics.caveat: No comparable Taiwanese system is publicly reported.
